question: In recent days, information has come to light about Azerbaijan preparing another attack against Armenia. President Aliyev has categorically denied that this is the case but the fact that he continues to build up forces close to the buffer zone and receive arms from Türkiye, would suggest the opposite.

Just a few months ago, I warned about the danger of Azeri forces carrying out a ground operation in Nagorno Karabakh with the aim of occupying the region. Most in the EU are refusing to open their eyes to Baku’s military preparations. This has led to the violent occupation of the region and the displacement of thousands of Armenians. In view of this: 1.
What steps is the Commission taking to protect Armenia from another potential act of aggression by Baku, spurred on by Ankara?

Is it looking at specific measures to make it clear to both Azerbaijan and Ankara that there will be a high price to pay, as far as the EU is concerned, in the event of any new act of aggression against Armenia?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.5.2024) The EU is committed to supporting a stable and peaceful future for the South Caucasus region. To this end, the EU has been engaged in the facilitation of the normalisation of relations between Armenia and Azerbaijan.

The EU has repeatedly called on Azerbaijan to re-engage towards sustainable peace and sent clear messages to the Azerbaijani authorities that any violation of Armenia’s territorial integrity would have consequences for EU-Azerbaijan relations. The EU encourages Azerbaijan to seize the momentum of the 29th Session of the Conference of Parties in Baku to come forward with a constructive agenda.

The EU has increased its efforts to support Armenia’s resilience, working together on a new ambitious Partnership Agenda, as a framework for boosting cooperation in all areas, and unlocking the full potential of the EU-Armenia Comprehensive and Enhanced Partnership Agreement1.

In the margins of the EU-United States-Armenia meeting in support of Armenia’s resilience on 5 April 2024, President of the Commission announced a EUR 270 million Resilience and Growth Plan for 2024-2027 in grant assistance to underpin the new Partnership Agenda. In the area of Common Security and Defence Policy, the EU and Armenia have agreed to scale up cooperation.

The Council already agreed in December 2023 to strengthen the EU Mission in Armenia, which is an essential component of the EU’s efforts in supporting peace in the region. The EU continues to support the normalisation of relations between Armenia and Türkiye, which would bring tangible benefits to both countries and to the whole region.
